verdict.rationale: Nix's own site advertises over 140,000 packages in Nixpkgs, and the official CLI includes `nix search` plus binary-cache downloads. Community reports independently confirm breadth: most apps listed as Homebrew-only are in Nixpkgs, and people use Nix to get package versions their distro lacks. Community caveats are that obscure packages sometimes need user wrapping and maintainers are stretched thin. Missing for 10: first-party evidence of how actively the repository is maintained (update cadence, maintainer count), and smoother coverage of obscure packages without users wrapping their own.

support.subject: As a developer, I can install almost anything I need from a large, actively maintained package registry or repository

citations.quote: Nix can automatically skip building from source and instead use a binary cache, a web server that provides pre-built binaries.
Most apps listed as Homebrew-only (Android Studio, tealdeer, Heroku CLI, Sublime Text, Slack, Postman) are in Nixpkgs.
